- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5%.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overbought traps.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment oscillating 0.3–0.6), model often fails to revert; force forecast to align with 10-day moving average if deviation > 2%.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in high-sentiment, low-liquidity periods; add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment >0.6 and price < recent 10-day low.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.6 to 0.2) and price is rising, model often fails to anticipate reversal; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days.
